College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 9, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
There are some key conference clashes on Saturday
By
Austin Nivison
Oct 31, 2026
at
12:05 pm ET
5 min read
Getty Images
We've made it to Week 9 of the college football season, and conference races are starting to really heat up. This weekend will create some separation with key games in the Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC.
The day starts with a huge Big 12 clash between No. 22 Arizona and No. 13 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, and the Wildcats are rolling. The pressure is on Texas Tech to get back on track, and Arizona is looking to prove itself against the best teams in the conference after losing to BYU earlier in the fall. The Wildcats at least have the quarterback edge with Noah Fifita playing at a high level.
In the afternoon, No. 3 Georgia plays No. 17 Florida in the World's Largest Indoor (?) Cocktail Party. Both rivals are coming off an open date, but their last games couldn't have been more different. Georgia was knocked off its No. 1 perch by Auburn, and Florida pulled off an upset against Texas. Will either of those results carry over to this game?
Elsewhere, No. 25 Wisconsin's trip to Iowa City will have major implications on the Big Ten race to the College Football Playoff, and No. 2 Ohio State goes to USC in what will be a major test for Lincoln Riley.
With so much football on at once, we've made a handy guide so you can prioritize your viewing experience.
The best games
No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech -- 12 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): The Red Raiders can't afford two consecutive losses, but here come the Wildcats with an upset on their minds. The vibes between these programs couldn't be any more different. Texas Tech super booster Cody Campbell is tweeting through it and threatening to restrict access for a local radio station. Meanwhile, Arizona coach Brent Brennan is buying shots for students after a blowout win over Iowa State. Unfortunately for the Wildcats, vibes alone don't win football games, and the Red Raiders will be desperate for a win.
No. 25 Wisconsin at Iowa -- 12 p.m. on Fox, Fubo (try for free): One week has really flipped the outlook on this Big Ten matchup. Wisconsin went from unranked to No. 25 following a big ranked win over USC, and the Badgers have all the momentum rolling into Iowa City. The Hawkeyes, on the other hand, lost the Floyd of Rosedale at the buzzer as Minnesota kicked its way to hog heaven. Now Iowa is unranked and looking to rebound by taking home the Heartland Trophy -- a giant brass bull. If you thought it couldn't get much more Big Ten than Minnesota vs. Iowa, strap in for this matchup on Saturday afternoon and watch these programs paint a masterpiece.
No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia -- 3:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): Depending upon the status of the Mercedes-Benz Stadium roof, the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party may be moving inside. What we know for sure is that this matchup has a lot of intrigue, with Florida coming off an enormous win over Texas and Georgia coming off a gut punch against Auburn. The biggest question about this rivalry matchup is what the Gators will do at quarterback. Sophomore Tramell Jones did enough to beat the Longhorns, but did he do enough to lock down the starting job over Aaron Philo, who struggled before suffering an injury? I would say you can't roll Jones out against an elite defense like Georgia, but he was fine against Texas.
Minnesota at No. 4 Indiana -- 3:30 p.m. on CBS, CBSSports.com, Paramount+ Premium: The spread for this game is enormous, which suggests it could be a get-right spot for Indiana. That said, the Hoosiers haven't exactly cruised through Big Ten play. They needed overtime to beat Michigan last week, although that game was on the road against a great defense. Neither of those things will be a factor on Saturday. Minnesota is coming off a huge rivalry win against Iowa, and now it has to face the defending champs on the road. The Golden Gophers will have to get something out of their abysmal run game (100.1 yards per game) to pull off the upset.
No. 6 Utah at Cincinnati -- 3:45 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): Can the Bearcats do it again? One week after handing Texas Tech its first loss, Cincinnati can do the same thing to Utah, which just beat Houston in a dramatic top-25 matchup. Cincy had a ton of success on the ground against the Red Raiders as it ran for 255 yards, but that will be much tougher to pull off against the Utes. That's because Utah ranks eighth nationally in rush defense, and the Bearcats will be in trouble if they have to rely on JC French's arm all game.
No. 2 Ohio State at USC -- 7:30 p.m. on NBC, Fubo (try for free): Lincoln Riley needs a big win in the worst way, and he's already lost to a backup quarterback once with Dylan Raiola carving up USC for most of that game against Oregon. The second-ranked Buckeyes will bring an inexperienced quarterback into L.A. Memorial Coliseum -- whether it's Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair. It's a prime opportunity for Riley to cool his seat and put his team in position for a run at the College Football Playoff. If USC loses, however, the pressure on Riley will be greater than ever. Jeremiah Smith can really strengthen his Heisman Trophy candidacy if he plays well without Julian Sayin in the lineup.

2026 WNBA Finals schedule: Dream cruise past Valkyries in Game 6, force first-ever Game 7
The Dream took care of business at home in Game 6, forcing the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history on Saturday in San Francisco
By
Lindsay Gibbs
Oct 29, 2026
at
4:30 pm ET
2 min read
Adam Eargle, CBS Sports
For the first time, the WNBA Finals are headed for a do-or-die Game 7.
The Golden State Valkyries had a chance to clinch their first title on Thursday, but the Atlanta Dream defended their home court with an 80-69 win in Game 6 to keep their season alive and force the series to shift back to the West Coast on Saturday.
The Dream, led by Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard and Angel Reese, jumped out to an early double-digit lead and never looked back. Gray led the way with 23 points while Howard had 21 and Reese posted another double-double with 15 points and 14 rebounds. For the Valkyries, Gabby Williams led all scorers with 26 points, but the team as a whole shot just 31% from the field.
To reach this stage, the Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces.
The Dream knocked the Washington Mystics out in the first round and are a perfect 5-0 in the playoffs. The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round, needing all three games to do so. The Finals, for the second season ever, are a best-of-seven series in 2026.
The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. Multiple regular-season records fell this year, from Clark becoming the first player in WNBA history with a 40-point, 10-assist game, to Angel Reese breaking the single-game rebounding record with 26 to Kelsey Mitchell passing A'ja Wilson's single-season points record.

Colts actively engaged in Jonathan Taylor trade talks: Five teams reportedly interested in star running back
The Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
By
Zachary Pereles
Oct 31, 2026
at
11:07 am ET
3 min read
Getty Images
The Indianapolis Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor and are actively engaging with teams about a deal, according to ESPN and NFL Network.
The news comes amid a Colts' fire sale that has seen Indianapolis (2-5) trade two cornerstones this week. The Colts traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick and traded DeForest Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick.
The return stands to be much bigger for Taylor. The Colts have already received at least one offer that includes a second-round pick plus additional compensation, per ESPN. Taylor, who said Thursday he's proud to wear the horseshoe and hasn't requested a trade, remains one of the league's most productive backs. He has twice led the NFL in rushing touchdowns, including last season, and led the league in rushing yards in 2021 on his way to first-team All-Pro honors. He has eight rushing touchdowns through seven games this year, putting him on pace to threaten his career high of 18.
ESPN reports the teams with at least some interest include the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants and Seahawks. Here's how each could fit:
Green Bay Packers
The Packers (5-3) recently got Josh Jacobs back from the commissioner-exempt list, but Green Bay's rushing struggles are reaching historic proportions. Green Bay is last in rushing yards per game (60.6) and yards per rush (2.9). The former is on pace to be the worst since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, the latter on pace to be the second-worst. That has put an enormous weight on quarterback Jordan Love: Currently, nearly 82% of Green Bay's yards have come via the pass, on pace for the highest rate since the merger.
New York Giants
John Harbaugh has fiddled with New York's running back rotation this season but is on the record that he would "love" a bell cow a la Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley on his team. The Giants (4-2-1) lead a wide-open NFC East, and Taylor could not only take the load off new starter J.J. McCarthy but also be a boon; playing next to Jaxson Dart would be an enticing look next year.  Cam Skattebo's bounce-back Week 7 performance after getting no touches in Week 6 might have placated previous backfield worries, but clearly New York is willing to poke around for an upgrade.
Denver Broncos
The Broncos (5-2) sent a first-round pick to Miami for Jaylen Waddle this offseason, though it hasn't really worked out yet. Would they make another big move, this time for a running back? Denver has struggled to muster much on the ground, which has only exacerbated Bo Nix's struggles. Broncos running backs rank 10th in yards before first contact per rush, suggesting good blocking, but 30th in yards after first contact per rush. Rookie Jonah Coleman has impressed but also dealt with injuries. Denver does have an extra fourth-round pick in 2027.
Seattle Seahawks
Seattle (4-3) already did business with Indianapolis this week, and perhaps reuniting Nelson with Taylor could be the boost their attempt for a second straight Super Bowl title needs. The Seahawks very much miss Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, and haven't found much on the ground without him. Zach Charbonnet is on his way back, as is first-round pick Jadarian Price, but Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have both had devastating fumbles in the interim. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was with the 49ers when they acquired Christian McCaffrey midseason, so he knows the value of a great top running back.
Minnesota Vikings
The Vikings are 6-0, but their 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions. Minnesota has moved the ball decently but hasn't found the finishing touch to get into the end zone. Taylor has 40 touchdowns over the past three seasons, the third-most in the NFL, and pairing him with a mobile quarterback like Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Minnesota also has draft capital to spare, including an extra third-round pick, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

articles.title: Luka Dončić teaches Yaxel Lendeborg a lesson, but Warriors bail their rookie out in comeback win over Lakers
articles.text:
Luka Dončić teaches Yaxel Lendeborg a lesson, but Warriors bail their rookie out - CBS Sports
site: media | arena: nba | pageType: stories |
section: | slug: luka-doncic-yaxel-lendeborg-warriors-comeback-win-lakers | sport: basketball | route: article_single.us |
6-keys: media/spln/nba/reg/free/stories
Skip to Main Content
NBA Standings
Power Rankings
Luka Dončić teaches Yaxel Lendeborg a lesson, but Warriors bail their rookie out in comeback win over Lakers
Lendeborg did not back up his Luka smack talk in the worst performance of his young career
By
Brad Botkin
Oct 31, 2026
at
12:25 pm ET
4 min read
Imagn Images
When Yaxel Lendeborg decided it would be a good idea to start a war of words with Luka Dončić during and after his first career NBA game, basically calling the Lakers superstar a flopping crybaby for whom he "lost all respect," both Stephen Curry and Steve Kerr had the same message for their brash rookie.
"Now you've got to back it up."
Friday night was Lendeborg's chance to do just that when the Warriors hosted Dončić and the Lakers for the start of the NBA Cup's group stage. It did not, to put it politely, go well for Lendeborg, who laid down the worst track of his young career with six points, one rebound, zero assists and five turnovers.
Why Yaxel Lendeborg could be the key to saving what's left of the Warriors' Stephen Curry era
Brad Botkin
Lendeborg got into early foul trouble and was never a factor on either end. For a guy who has injected so much juice into what looked like an old, disinterested, almost lifeless Warriors team when it faced these same Lakers on opening night, Lendeborg was all but invisible in finishing as a game-low minus-20 in his 24 minutes before fouling out.
When asked what lesson he had taken from a performance like this after shining such a spotlight on himself with the Luka comments, and what he might do differently next time, Lendeborg, with the same brutal honest he has shown at every turn, said he would "try not to wet the bed as bad as I did."
Meanwhile, Dončić -- who was egging on the "Luka sucks!" chant coming from the Chase Center crowd early on -- poured in 21 first-quarter points en route to 37 for the game. He added seven rebounds, five assists, a pair of blocks and a steal for good measure. He outscored the entire Warriors team in the first quarter by himself as the Lakers raced out to a 25-point first-half lead.
Luka Doncic’s face after hitting a 3 over Yaxel Lendeborg 😂 pic.twitter.com/CAiF7LUxDz— Lake Show (@LakeShowFamily) October 31, 2026
Certainly everything you've read so far would suggest the Lakers ran away with this game, but in today's NBA, a 20-point lead is just prologue for a second-half plot twist. And sure enough, the Warriors, behind eight 3-pointers and 31 points from Curry, stormed back to win going away, 112-95, for their third straight victory after opening the season 0-3.
Lendeborg might not have been able to back up his Dončić talk (which, we have to point out, was nothing but the truth, even if you could argue he would've been better off keeping it to himself, at least this early in his career), but the greatest shooter to ever set foot on this planet had his back. This is how you go at Luka Dončić ...
A 3PT MASTERCLASS FROM STEPHEN
📺 @NBAonPrime pic.twitter.com/nIIyrtmuKM— Golden State Warriors (@warriors) October 31, 2026
And this ...
STOP IT, STEPH 🥵 pic.twitter.com/8ns53YenN2— Warriors on NBCS (@NBCSWarriors) October 31, 2026
It wasn't just Curry -- who passed Dominique Wilkins for 18th on the NBA's all-time scoring list -- coming to Lendeborg's rescue. It was Brandin Podziemski with 21 points, six assists and five rebounds. It was De'Anthony Melton and Georges Niang tag-teaming for 27 points and seven 3-pointers. It was Draymond Green taking over the Dončić defensive duties and dishing out nine dimes. It was the Warriors' bench outscoring L.A.'s bench 50-7, and a defense that held the Lakers to just 57 points over the final three quarters to fuel an astounding 42-point turnaround.
For Lendeborg, there's a lesson here that goes beyond not riling up a superstar and letting your play do the talking (which, I will restate, was fine; he's a grown man, and he didn't say anything that everyone else doesn't think), which is that it ultimately doesn't matter that Dončić got the better of him individually on Friday, because in the end it was the Warriors that got the better of the Lakers.
This was the message that Kerr had for Lendeborg after the opener in which Lendeborg was all too proud of his individual defense on Dončić.
"He did a good job on Luka one-on-one, but we got torched by Luka as a team," Kerr said. "All those stats that the NBA puts up, like, 'Hey, when he guarded him, who the eff cares?' It's like, they scored 127 on us. That stuff's all bulls---. It's our defense."
Translation: it's a team game. As his career progresses, Lendeborg, a clear alpha, is going to be the one picking up his teammates on plenty of nights, but on this night it was the rookie who needed his teammates to cover for him. Suffice it to say, they did that, and Lendeborg, to his credit, recognized the effort with genuine humility.
"Them boys had my back today," Lendeborg said, noting that in his effort to stay calm and not let the hype of the matchup take over, he actually stayed "a little too calm" and never got into a groove. "Steph Curry, again, did his thing. The bench mob showed up today. It was awesome. They all played a great game. I feel like I was the only Debbie downer on the team. I feel like next time I get into one of these games, just try to be that guy sucking up all the energy."

Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP
Kucherov's days with the Lightning appear to be over
By
Austin Nivison
Oct 30, 2026
at
9:57 pm ET
5 min read
Getty Images
One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.
Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.
Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.
Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.
It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.
Montreal Canadiens
Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.
Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.
Minnesota Wild
We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.
However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.
With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.
Carolina Hurricanes
It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.
Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?
Utah Mammoth
Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.
Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.
Dallas Stars
Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-yea

College football picks: Predictions against the spread, odds, betting lines for top 25 games in Week 9
A closer look at the top games on tap Saturday as college football Week 9 takes center stage
By
John Talty
Oct 31, 2026
at
12:15 pm ET
5 min read
Getty Images
It's dangerous being ranked near the top of the polls. Three top-two teams have lost to unranked opponents over the last three weeks, a first since the carnage that was the 2007 season.
Texas fell, Georgia tripped and BYU was overwhelmed.
Now, No. 1 Miami and No. 2 Ohio State both hit the road this week against unranked teams. At least for Miami, the Hurricanes have history on their side. They're 30-0 all-time against unranked opponents as the AP's No. 1 team. They travel to North Carolina, which is 0-11 all-time against the nation's No. 1 team. If Miami can get past Bill Belichick's Tar Heels, a marquee matchup awaits next week at Notre Dame.
No team is safe as parity runs rampant nationwide. Coach Mario Cristobal said there's no sense in letting up this week.
"If not, you're putting a win at risk," he said.
Meanwhile, Ohio State enters a road trip to USC with a problem. The Buckeyes still haven't announced a starting quarterback to replace Julian Sayin, who is out indefinitely. Luke Fahey, who replaced Sayin late in the win against Indiana, and former five-star Tavian St. Clair battled for the starting gig during the bye week. Both could play. If so, Fahey will play near his home in Mission Viejo, California. USC needs a win as questions about coach Lincoln Riley's future swirl.
We enter Week 9 with only three unbeaten teams — Miami, No. 7 UCLA and No. 6 Utah. That's the fewest this early in a season since 1977. Utah goes to Cincinnati, which just beat then-undefeated Texas Tech and can become the first unranked team since 1938 St. Mary's to beat ranked teams at 6-0 or better in back-to-back games.
Minnesota, holder of all three of its rivalry trophies for the first time since 1978, visits No. 4 Indiana, which hasn't scored 21 points in three straight games.
We also have a monster rivalry game as No. 3 Georgia plays No. 17 Florida in Atlanta for the first time in the rivalry's history. The Bulldogs are coming off a bye week after losing at home to unranked Auburn. Georgia is trying to avoid becoming only the second No. 1 team in history to lose back-to-back games.
The other team was Texas, and it happened this month.
College football in 2026 is a different kind of beast. Here's how the CBS Sports experts see it developing in Week 9, the final Saturday of the regular season without the College Football Playoff rankings.
Minnesota vs. Indiana prediction, picks
3:30 p.m. on CBS  CBSSports.com,  CBS Sports App  Paramount+ Premium: If it ain't broke, don't fix it. The Hoosiers are quite simply an under machine right now. It's not just that they have an elite defense and a sputtering offense, but it's the way Curt Cignetti is managing games. The lack of trust in Hoover is never more apparent than when he trots the punt unit out on a fourth-and-short at midfield without hesitation. Even if Indiana dominates, it's hard to see them piling up points on a good Minnesota defense, and there's a real world where the Gophers keep this close throughout. Either way, it'll come down to the team that converts opportunities into touchdowns rather than field goals, and this total is a bit too high at 40. Pick: UNDER 41.5

Super Bowl stock report for Week 8: Joe Burrow's excellence ignites Bengals, Texans reach screeching halt
We assess the NFL title race after Week 7 and identify four upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
By
Carter Bahns
Oct 29, 2026
at
7:30 am ET
6 min read
Getty Images
None of the three Super Bowl favorites (the San Francisco 49ers, Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs) added wins to their tally last week, which goes to show how open the championship race is in Week 8. There is still time for teams further down the pecking order to either make up ground on the frontrunners or surpass them entirely in the divisional and Wild Card standings before the postseason hunt really heats up in the second half of the campaign.
That means the Cincinnati Bengals have ample opportunities to take command of an AFC North that might surprisingly be the most competitive division in football. On the other hand, the clock is ticking much faster on the Houston Texans than anyone thought possible heading into the season.
A plethora of top-tier Super Bowl contenders will go head-to-head this week, which will either separate the most formidable title hopefuls from the rest or cloud the picture even further.
Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race heading into Week 8.
Super Bowl odds entering Week 8
Odds via DraftKings, +2000 or better
49ers: +580
Bills: +700
Chiefs: +900
Seahawks: +1000
Rams: +1100
Jaguars: +1200
Ravens: +1300

Bengals: +1600
Vikings: +1700
Patriots: +1900
Broncos: +1900
Stock up: Joe Burrow's excellence ignites Bengals
It took until Week 7 for them to earn their first divisional win, but that was all it took for the Bengals to become the AFC North favorites for the first time this season. At halftime, when they trailed the Ravens, 13-0, it looked as though they were bound to fall to 0-2 in the uber-competitive division. But then Joe Burrow happened. The superstar quarterback posted a perfect passer rating across the third and fourth quarters when he completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns. It was perhaps the best half of his terrific career.
The offense has been consistent throughout the first two months of the year and now has back-to-back games with at least 31 points. The defense has shown flashes of improvement following multiple years of misery, but it has yet to string together strong showings. If that comes by season's end, the Bengals will be a complete team with a top-flight quarterback and a sometimes unstoppable offense. That defensive unit has to prove itself before Cincinnati can be taken seriously as a Super Bowl contender, but again, the signs are there. It stifled Tyler Huntley in a shutout second half on Sunday and, in Week 2, held the Texans to just six points.
Burrow showed last week that he can still make up for many of the defense's shortcomings. He did so a week prior with four touchdowns in an eerily close game against the Miami Dolphins, too. Cincinnati is getting peak Burrow right now. It needs to capitalize.
Stock down: Texans' resurgence reaches screeching halt
The Texans' chances of becoming the second team in NFL history to bounce back from an 0-4 start and reach the playoffs took a major hit. Allowing J.J. McCarthy to log the third-best start of his maligned young career (by passer rating) was the latest example of how a defense expected to be the league's best has regressed into a state of unexplainable dysfunction. The two long runs in overtime —  Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary broke off to win the game for the New York Giants — were uncharacteristic of the kind of rushing plays Houston is wont to surrender, too.
DeMeco Ryans' defense was the stingiest in the NFL last season by yards allowed and ranked second in scoring. This season, the unit stands in the bottom half of the league in both metrics. If it held up its end of the bargain, imagine where the Texans would be. C.J. Stroud is playing his way to a massive contract extension but cannot get a lick of help on the other side of the ball. A year ago, the story was the complete opposite. It is hard to make sense of why this role reversal has occurred, given that the roster is mostly the same as in 2025 and the coaching staff did not experience any meaningful turnover either.
Long shot of the week: Cowboys (+3200)
Until they show that they can slow their opponents down more effectively, the Dallas Cowboys will remain only a fringe contender for a deep playoff run. They still have yet to hold a team under 20 points. Even the depleted Philadelphia Eagles reached the end zone three times against them.
But something clicked offensively for the Cowboys on "Monday Night Football" and rejuvenated a unit that had been anemic the previous two weeks. Javonte Williams has leveled up this season and is now the NFL's rushing touchdown leader after a 155-yard explosion against the bitter-rival Eagles. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens accounted for three touchdowns in the road win and might be back in form as a terrorizing duo at receiver. If that was the start of a dominant run for an offense capable of competing among the NFL's best, then Dallas might be the team to beat in the downtrodden and wide-open NFC East.
Week 8 games to watch
Ravens at Bills
Sunday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
The ongoing uncertainty surrounding Lamar Jackson's ankle places a dark cloud over the Ravens and their potential to reach the playoffs. Even if he returns in Week 8, his team will be in great danger of dropping a third consecutive game. The Bills enter the showdown off a bye and will be positioned well
